batchName: Empire: Diocletian and Constantine (AD 284-337) - Medium Batch 2

questions.question: According to a Christian teacher in Nicomedia, who pushed for harsher measures against Christians than Diocletian wanted?
questions.explanation: The Christian teacher blamed Galerius, the junior emperor in the East, for pressing for harsher persecution. In the West, Maximian and Constantine's father ignored the later edicts.
questions.sourceQuote: According to a Christian teacher living in Nicomedia, Galerius, the junior emperor in the East, pushed for harsher measures than Diocletian wanted.

questions.question: What happened at Antioch in 299 that set the persecution of Christians in motion?
options: Christians burned a temple of Jupiter
A Christian soldier attacked the emperor
Diviners said the omens failed and blamed Christians
A bishop publicly insulted the emperor
Christian merchants refused to pay new taxes
questions.explanation: Priests who read the future in animals' entrails said the signs had failed and blamed Christians at court. Courtiers and soldiers were then ordered to sacrifice or be dismissed.
questions.sourceQuote: In 299 at Antioch, priests who read the future in animals' entrails said the signs had failed and blamed Christians at court.

questions.question: What was 'adoratio' at Diocletian's court?
options: Senators kissing the emperor's gold crown
Priests offering sacrifice for the emperor
Soldiers swearing a yearly oath to Jupiter
Visitors lying face down before the emperor
Crowds chanting praise at imperial games
questions.explanation: Under adoratio, visitors had to lie face down before the emperor. Diocletian also wore a gold crown and jewels to raise himself above ordinary mortals.
questions.sourceQuote: Diocletian wore a gold crown and jewels, and visitors had to lie face down before him (*adoratio*).

questions.question: In the earliest account of Constantine's vision, written by a Christian teacher, what was Constantine told in a dream?
options: To paint a sign of Christ on his soldiers' shields
To spare Maxentius if he surrendered
To march on Rome before the new moon
To build a great church in Rome
questions.explanation: The Christian teacher wrote that on the night before the battle Constantine dreamed he should paint a heavenly sign of Christ on his soldiers' shields. A bishop's later biography told a grander story of a cross in the sky.
questions.sourceQuote: Lactantius, a Christian teacher writing soon afterwards, said that the night before the battle, Constantine was told in a dream to paint a heavenly sign of Christ on his soldiers' shields.

questions.question: Which river did Maxentius have at his back at the Milvian Bridge?
questions.explanation: Maxentius drew up his army with the Tiber behind it, beside the bridge that carried the main road from the north into Rome. He also added a temporary bridge of boats.
questions.sourceQuote: He drew up his army with the Tiber at its back, beside the Milvian Bridge, which carried the main road from the north into Rome, and added a temporary bridge of boats.

questions.question: Who ran each of the twelve dioceses created by Diocletian?
options: A frontier general called a dux
A proconsul named by the Senate
questions.explanation: Diocletian grouped the provinces into twelve dioceses, each run by a deputy called a vicarius. This added a new layer to the largest government Rome had ever known.
questions.sourceQuote: They were grouped into twelve regions called dioceses, each run by a deputy (*vicarius*).

questions.question: What rank did Galerius grudgingly grant Constantine in 306?
questions.explanation: The troops at York had proclaimed Constantine Augustus, but Galerius recognised him only as the junior Caesar. Three months later Maxentius seized Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: Galerius grudgingly recognised him only as Caesar.

questions.question: Who was blamed when fires broke out in the imperial palace at Nicomedia?
questions.explanation: After the palace fires, Christians were blamed, tortured and executed. It became the last, largest and bloodiest attack on Christians by the Roman state.
questions.sourceQuote: After fires broke out in the palace, Christians were blamed, tortured and executed.

questions.question: Near which river did Diocletian defeat the western emperor in 285?
questions.explanation: Diocletian, newly proclaimed in the East, defeated the western emperor in 285 near the river Margus in modern Serbia.
questions.sourceQuote: Renamed Diocletian, he defeated the western emperor in 285 near the river Margus in modern Serbia.

questions.question: What special role did the city of Nisibis gain under the peace of 299?
options: The new capital of the Persian kings
The only trading point between the empires
The seat of the restored Armenian king
A Roman naval base on the Tigris
questions.explanation: Nisibis became the only trading point between Rome and Persia. The Peace of Nisibis also brought Armenia back under Roman influence and proved lasting.
questions.sourceQuote: The Peace of Nisibis in 299, named after a frontier city that became the only trading point between the empires, brought Armenia back under Roman influence.
